title: The Trojan Women
subtitle: The morning after Troy — what victory costs the losers

learningObjectives.text: What does the play show about the cost of victory?
What happens to Troy's royal women?

main.author: Euripides
main.locator: Trojan Women, Poseidon’s opening speech; Coleridge TEI body, passage on Scamander’s banks and allocation of captives
main.excerpt: desolation seizes on a town, the worship of the gods decays and tends to lose respect. Scamander’s banks re-echo long and loud the screams of captive maids, as they by lot receive their masters. Arcadia takes some, and some the people of Thessaly; others are assigned to Theseus’ sons, the Athenian chiefs.

narrativeBlocks.title: The city already fallen
narrativeBlocks.body: The Trojan Women opens after the sack — the Greeks have won, the heroes are dead, and the city is ash. The play has no war left: only the division of the spoils.

narrativeBlocks.title: Hecuba's ledger
narrativeBlocks.body: Queen Hecuba, who watched her husband and sons die, is now counted as property. The Greeks parcel out the royal women as slaves and concubines: Cassandra to Agamemnon, Andromache to Achilles's son, Hecuba to Odysseus — the man she once helped deceive.

narrativeBlocks.title: The last child of Troy
narrativeBlocks.body: The play's unbearable centre: Astyanax, Hector's infant son, is taken from Andromache's arms and thrown from the walls — the Greeks will not let a Trojan prince grow up. Hecuba buries the future of Troy.

narrativeBlocks.title: A warning to the audience
narrativeBlocks.body: The Athenian audience watching this was itself an empire that had just destroyed a neutral island's men and enslaved its women. Euripides makes them watch what that looks like from below.

narrativeBlocks.title: Victors write, but survivors remember
narrativeBlocks.body: Everything the Greeks 'won' at Troy sits on a pile of widows and orphans — the plays keep both the victory and the bill visible. The same war the Iliad made glorious, Euripides prices in the same coin.

quiz.prompt: What does The Trojan Women focus on that the Iliad does not?

choices.text: The aftermath for the defeated — the enslaved women and murdered heir of a sacked city, not the victors' glory
The gods' quarrels over the war
The siege strategies of the Greeks

quiz.explanation: Euripides deliberately shows the cost side of the same war the Iliad epicises.

choices.text: He is thrown from the walls by the Greeks — no Trojan prince will be allowed to grow up
He dies in the siege already

quiz.explanation: The killing of Hector's infant son is the play's moral bottom line: victory that requires this is not clean.
